Definition: from G4012 and G4685; to drag all around, i.e. (figuratively) to distract (with care):--cumber.
BiblicalUsage: Perispao means to be dragged about, distracted, cumbered. Martha was cumbered about much serving, and she came to Jesus and said, “Lord, dost thou not care that my sister hath left me to serve alone? Bid her therefore that she help me.”
TheologicalSignificance: I am convinced that Martha's trouble was not her serving but her cumbering: she was dragged about by much serving, and she blamed the one who sat still.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
